news.title: SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters
news.summary_raw:
AI agents often fail because their instructions, or skills, are manually modified with no guarantee of improvement. Learn how SkillOpt turns skill editing into a training process, making agent behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
The post SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed SkillOpt, a technique to turn agent skills into trainable parameters. This makes agent behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
news.enterprise_use: Note that SkillOpt has potential applications in automating agent behavior in IT workflows, such as service desk bots or ticket routing, and consider reviewing its research in the next 90 days for potential value in your toolset.

news.title: Tencent's Apache-licensed Hy3 takes on GLM-5.2 at half the size — and wins everywhere except coding
news.summary_raw: For the past year, the awkward secret of the open-weight model boom has been that many of the strongest Chinese releases were off-limits to a large slice of the enterprises most interested in them. License terms that excluded the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea meant legal teams killed deployments before engineering teams finished their evals — not just for companies headquartered there, but for any enterprise serving traffic into those regions. For IT teams weighing open mode
news.summary: Tencent has released Apache-licensed open-weight model Hy3, which outperforms GLM-5.2 but only in regions with more relaxed licensing.
news.enterprise_use: Check your organization's current open-weight model usage and assess the potential risks of switching to a more open-licensed model like Hy3, especially if you serve traffic in restricted regions; most affected tool: AWS/Azure infrastructure.

news.title: Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
news.summary_raw:
AI agents can't remember past conversations. They must constantly reload or retrieve context, which grows less efficient as tasks get longer and more complex. Memora solves this with a scalable memory system separating what’s stored from how it's retrieved.
The post Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed Memora, a scalable memory system that balances abstraction and specificity for AI agents. Memora separates what's stored from how it's retrieved, improving efficiency in longer and more complex tasks.
news.enterprise_use: This doesn't directly affect your current IT stack, but note that Memora could lead to advancements in conversational AI and potentially impact future interactions with AI-powered tools.
